rationale: The alias qualifier (`global::`) is not part of a name. This lane publishes the FULL dotted path for a type target, so a source file that writes `global::A.B` must publish the same target as the twin that writes `A.B` — and before this round it published the qualifier instead. Measured on BOTH pinned corpora, over all 76 files containing `::` (script/m14/tmp/cs-alias-qualifier-census.ts): 146 rows carried the qualifier — 49 `instantiates`, 2 `extends`, and 95 ATTRIBUTE names in the decorator payload — and the row-level before/after is exact: 146 rows removed, 146 added, every removed row a twin of an added row at the same file+type+line with only the qualifier stripped, 0 unexplained and 0 fabricated (script/m14/tmp/cs-alias-row-dump.ts; decorator rows are dumped UNFILTERED because a filter on `::` hides the post-fix spelling and makes the reconciliation unverifiable). R10 independently moved on the same change (`sep=1 unruled=instantiates|:` before, `sep=0 unruled=-` after), and the differential's csharp lane is byte-identical before and after at full corpus extent (fsharp: 243 files, 12,886/12,886, MISSING=0, unexplained=0, same file-set hash `4d0e5ba230a7b27f`). The corpora exercise only creation, heritage and attributes, so the REST of this fixture comes from probing every type-name position the language has (script/m14/tmp/cs-alias-position-battery.ts, -battery2.ts, -battery3.ts, -battery4.ts, cs-alias-single-segment-probe.ts), which is how it came to cover the four positions a corpus measurement cannot see — the using directive's module, the target-typed `new()` resolved from a qualified declared type, the conversion OPERATOR's name (a SYMBOL name, which never passes through the type-name cleaning the relationship targets do), and the plain `using global::System;` form — plus three positions where the shape published NOTHING AT ALL rather than the wrong spelling: explicit `new global::Root()`, a method return type, and an indexer's return type. Those three share one root cause: a hardcoded node list omitting `alias_qualified_name`, the node the pinned grammar gives a `global::`-qualified name with a SINGLE segment (it is wrapped in a `qualified_name` only when a dot follows the qualifier). The corpora contain 550 multi-segment occurrences and 0 single-segment ones, so no draw could ever have seen it; the fixture is the only instrument that can hold those positions. EVERY row here is written TWICE — qualified and unqualified — so the expected spelling is read off the twin rather than asserted by hand. SOURCE-SPELLING CORRECTION 2026-10-02: the type-level edges are pinned with the BARE type name as the relationship source (`Widget`, `Shape`, `Qualified`), not the namespace-qualified one (`Pin.Widget`, `Acme.Domain.Shape`, `Probe.Qualified`) these rows used to name. The analyzer publishes the bare name, and the hand-audited truth agrees: validation/m12/ground-truth/csharp.json (truthSource=manual_audit) records type-level rows with bare sourceIds such as `BaseService -> BaseService {extends}` and `BaseService -> IRepository {implements}`. The qualified spelling was a pin that could never match, which is why this fixture was RED. Only the source LABEL changed: the edge type, target, line_number and every `meta.*` constraint are untouched, and the `forbid` rows that carried the qualified spelling were vacuous before (no edge ever had that source) and are now ACTIVE. Mutant csharp/drop-implements-edge and csharp/iface-base-extends-fabrication were unobservable for exactly this reason.
